blocks.text: Theme 1.2 · Source market growth and diversification · Focus area 5
The mature markets already pay the most and fill the fullest routes, so growth there comes from more value per visitor and more seats on existing routes, not from more marketing.
**December 2025.** Increase Yield in Mature Markets (UK, Europe, N. America) (Current State Diagnostic, Dec 2025, p64).

**October 2026: Validated, without fare or yield data.** Full routes. The October title drops the list of markets. MIDAS drove the disposition: the mature long-haul routes run above 80% load, and carriers on full routes raise fares before they add seats.

blocks.message: The highest-spending visitors come from the slowest-growing markets on the fullest routes.

blocks.text: The yield lever rests on MIDAS's reading of carrier behaviour, and no deliverable models a yield uplift. The entry therefore sets yield as an indicator to establish, not a target to hit, until spend per visitor by market is tracked every year [yield baseline: SAT spend per visitor by market as an annual series; only 2024 is printed].

Wesgro should protect share and raise value per visitor in the mature markets, and work the full routes for frequency and gauge before it chases new ones. The Demand-Side Analysis frames the job as protecting share, increasing yield and driving regional dispersal while new growth markets are developed (Demand-Side Analysis, Jun 2026, p17). MIDAS sees tactical room for added frequency on some routes and larger aircraft from some airlines (MIDAS Aviation Market Assessment, Mar 2026, In Conclusion).

rows: Make the case to carriers on the five full routes for added frequency or larger aircraft, backed by green-season marketing
Sell Discerning Connoisseur product through luxury advisors and high-end operators in the UK, USA, Germany, France and Switzerland
Add a yield measure, spend per visitor by market with length of stay, beside arrivals in Wesgro's own targets
Invest in premium product outside the Metro and in the midscale branded accommodation the province lacks (focus areas 11 and 15)
Escalate the cap on US carriers, the absence of an Open Skies agreement and the bilateral agreements that limit airlift

blocks.text: New Zealand runs yield-based performance, putting revenue per visitor and length of stay ahead of arrivals growth and selling premium regional itineraries through specialist travel designers (Global Benchmarking Report, Mar 2026, p55). Its total visitor spend grew 9.2% in the year to March 2025, against arrivals growth of 5.9% (p53).

**Initiative I1**, segment-led activation and yield in mature markets (section 4.3), with the frequency case run under **I6** (focus area 7). **Indicators** T1-03 direct foreign spend at impact level and T2-07 mature-market spend per visitor at outcome level (section 5.2).
